_readme: Single source of truth for the pool the platform names tabs from. The worker picks from it whenever a caller opens an agent or a terminal without a title (the CLI, the quick-open buttons, ChangeBranchDialog); the New Agent and New Terminal dialogs pick from the same table to pre-fill their Title field. Both sides generate from this file -- Go reads contracts.TabNames, the browser reads TAB_NAMES -- so the two can never drift. A title is `<prefix> <name>`, joined with one space: `Agent Gabe`, `Terminal Tim`. plan_mode.go builds its auto-title regex from titlePrefixes.agent, so a name that stops matching ^[A-Z][A-Za-z]+$ would silently disable plan-mode auto-rename; the schema refuses one.
_rules: Six rules decide what goes in. 1 SHAPE: ^[A-Z][A-Za-z]+$, 2 to 8 characters, no hyphen or apostrophe or accent. 2 FRIENDLY FORM ONLY: when everyday usage shortens a name, the pool carries the short form alone -- William gives Bill, Robert gives Bob, Theodore gives Theo, Isabella gives Bella, Harriet gives Hattie. A name usage does not shorten (Noah, Mia, Isla, Luna, Mateo) stays whole. Bill and Will both stay: they differ at the first letter, the position a reader scans. 3 ONE SPELLING PER NAME: Sophie not Sofia, Luca not Luka, Zoe not Zoey, Jaxon not Jaxson. 4 PREDICTABLE PRONUNCIATION: drop a name whose English pronunciation the spelling does not give -- Niamh, Esme, Cassius, Xavier, Gael, Jose, Ayla, Thea, Lucia, Ottilie. 5 DISTINCT AT A GLANCE: drop one of any pair a reader must look twice at -- Lyla beats Lila and Lilah, Mila beats Myla, Amara beats Amira, Audrey beats Aubrey. 6 NO IDENTITY MARKER: a name whose dominant reading is a specific religious figure or a religious or national symbol does not belong on a randomly-assigned scratch terminal, so Muhammad, Zion, Krishna and Jesus are out. That rule is about the FIGURE, not the language: Mateo, Camila and Amir are ordinary given names and stay, and a religious origin that naturalized into everyday English (Noah, Adam, Sarah, John, Micah, Genesis) is not a marker. Santiago and Genesis are kept deliberately, though one is `Saint James` and the other a book of the Bible, because neither reads that way in use. Rules 1 and 3 are mechanical and the schema plus checkTabNames enforce them. Rules 2, 4, 5 and 6 are judgment, and NO check can hold them -- a reviewer applies them at edit time.
